text:
Maria: heads-up, seeing a spike of CUDA illegal memory access + container OOMs on node gpu-qlk2. Pods are restarting, node is flapping. Root logs show "misaligned device address" during pagewalks.
incident-bot: Incident created INC-1767801234 · Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/serving/cuda-illegal-memory · severity: P2 · notified: oncall@sre.redwood (pager).
Ashwin: @Maria thanks. Can you paste `kubectl describe` for the failing pod and recent kubelet logs? Do we need to cordon the node now? :eyes:
Maria: kubectl get pods -n serving | grep gpu-qlk2
```
pod-ml-1        CrashLoopBackOff   1/5   3m
pod-embed       Running            1/1   10m
pod-router      Running            1/1   11m
```
Maria: `kubectl describe pod pod-ml-1` shows OOM + last termination message: `cuda: illegal memory access`
Eve: CS: rolling reports from customers — 4 tenants with increased 502s, roughly 1.8% of global requests in the last 5m. Two enterprise customers (acct-118, acct-224) flagged. Informing them now.
Kyle: Taking pager. Immediate plan: (1) cordon gpu-qlk2 (kubectl cordon gpu-qlk2) (2) drain best-effort non-critical pods (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data) (3) enable fallback pool routing for new sessions. I'll coordinate traffic shift.
Ashwin: Pulled container logs — stack snippet below. Looks like an async CUDA copy blamed on an invalid pointer after a page evict.
```
E0322 12:34:56.789 kernel: NVRM: Xid (31) 0000000a at 0x7f2b6a8d1000
E0322 12:34:56.790 serving: cuda: illegal memory access at 0x7ffdeadbeef in /opt/serving/model.so
backtrace:
 0x7f8c1a4f1a model_infer+0x123
 0x7f8c1a4f8b cudamemcpyasync_wrapper+0x45
 0x7f8c1a50c0 batcher_execute+0x2b
```
Maria: Repro hypothesis: cudaMemcpyAsync called with a stale KV-cache pointer after eviction or after a rapid reload -> misaligned deviceaddr. Could be a race between eviction path and async copy completion.
Ashwin: Short-term mitigation suggestions: disable batching on the affected model to force synchronous copies, reduce max_concurrency to drain async inflight copies, and avoid driver churn. Long-term: add pointer-ownership guards in the runtime.
Kyle: I'm cordoning gpu-qlk2 and starting drain now. Will collect core/vmcore before reboot.
Maria: Collecting artifacts and uploading to S3: `tar czf /tmp/1767801234.tgz /var/log/kern* /var/log/containers/* /proc/vmcore` then `aws s3 cp /tmp/1767801234.tgz s3://redwood-incidents/1767801234/` — doing that now.
incident-bot: Pager escalated to SRE Pager (level 2) at 12:40 UTC. Customer impact: partial degradation, fallback in progress.
SRE Pager: Acknowledged. I'll open a vendor ticket with GPU supplier (attach logs) and prepare a hotpatch path: reproduce in isolated docker with patched kernel module & instrument cudaMemcpy wrappers. Will also enable route-to-cpu fallback for new sessions until we have a driver/patch.
Eve: Drafting customer status message: "We detected an internal GPU runtime error that caused intermittent errors for a subset of requests. We have diverted traffic and are investigating. We will update within 30 minutes." Pushing to status.redwood and CS.
Ashwin: For reproduction, building a small repro container that runs repeated async copies + eviction pattern. Adding LD_PRELOAD wrapper around cudaMemcpy to log pointers. If repro succeeds we can submit minimal test to vendor.
Kyle: Node drained; affected pods rescheduled to fallback GPU-less pool. Monitoring error rate.
Maria: Error rate dropped from 1.8% to 0.4% after drain and routing to fallback pool. CPU latency higher but acceptable. Assigning postmortem owners: Maria + Ashwin. Next steps: reproduce, vendor escalation, runtime guard change, and a canaryed driver/patch rollout.
Eve: Customer notifications sent to impacted accounts; support tickets updated. :white_check_mark:
Kyle: Closing immediate mitigation. Incident remains open for follow-up and postmortem. Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/serving/cuda-illegal-memory.
